# Same voice, English

The profile's verbose-formal register carried into English. Three turns keep
the will but ask for criteria; only the last one is an explicit creation
command.

## Turn 1 — author
> How do I keep the reader wanting them after both leads confess in chapter
> three? The pull has to outlive the confession or the last two hundred pages
> are dead air.

- **Class:** `answer`
- **Offer expected:** no
- **Must not:** open a guided session; answer with a generic list of romance
  tropes
- **Why:** rule 2 — a question wins over anything else (tie-breaker 1)

## Turn 2 — author
> I need Renata's love interest to be a man who never raises his voice, and the
> chemistry still has to burn — any ideas?

- **Class:** `answer`
- **Offer expected:** yes — non-blocking, after the reply
- **Must not:** open a guided session; treat "I need" as a command and skip the
  reply
- **Why:** rule 2 — request for ideas; the volition is real but the question
  beats it (tie-breaker 1)

## Turn 3 — author
> The foreclosure afternoon is the engine of the whole book; everything else has
> to grow out of that one scene.

- **Class:** `answer`
- **Offer expected:** no
- **Must not:** open a guided session; turn a statement about the book into a
  character sheet
- **Why:** rule 2 — a statement about the author's own material is conversation

## Turn 4 — author
> Create Renata's love interest with your method, starting from the foreclosure
> and building him out of that contradiction.

- **Class:** `start_flow`
- **Target:** `guided-character`
- **Explicitness:** `imperative`
- **Must not:** answer with advice only; drop the foreclosure as the seed
  material
- **Why:** rule 5 — explicit command, no uncertainty and no request for input
